company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS estimates at $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the quality was low — the beat was driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, a market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80-90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex directly in the high-growth robotics and Physical AI space.

MillerKnoll reported solid FQ1 EPS of 53 cents vs. the Street at 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even excluding tariff refund tailwinds of 11 cents, implying clean EPS of 42 cents vs. 36 cents expected. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the $943.2 million consensus, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed slightly while EPS guidance was left unchanged, and the FQ2 EPS midpoint of 46 cents is in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through the transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a straightforward leadership transition with no financial results or guidance update.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, as gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the 13.85% expected, with management citing stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure squeezing consumers. Revenue came in at $2.311 billion, down 8.4% but above the $2.17 billion estimate. Some bright spots include healthy dealer inventory levels and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in North American towable RV order backlog, though the company will not provide formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. This is a significant data readout in the highly competitive and closely watched obesity drug space. The results position Viking as a credible competitor in the GLP-1 market.

sectors: RV sector faces headwinds per THOR Industries commentary — stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation are pressuring consumer budgets and keeping retail soft. Robotics and Physical AI are in focus with the Cognex-RealSense deal highlighting continued consolidation in vision technology.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd with no broad macro or Fed commentary included — just six names reporting before the open that traders need to know.

Starting with AutoZone. They beat on earnings per share, fifty-six dollars and five cents versus the Street at fifty-four dollars and three cents, but don't get excited — this was a low-quality beat. A 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit inflated gross margins. Strip those out and the picture gets ugly fast. Domestic comps came in at plus one point six percent, well short of the plus three point one percent expected, and the operating expense ratio worsened by 100 basis points year-over-year. Management says linearity improved through the quarter and they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027, but the core business clearly disappointed. Treat this as mixed at best.

Cognex is buying RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI, for roughly five hundred million upfront plus another hundred and six million. RealSense is expected to generate eighty to ninety million in revenue, growing more than fifty percent year-over-year. This is a direct bet on the robotics and Physical AI buildout — bullish for Cognex's long-term positioning.

MillerKnoll printed a clean beat — fifty-three cents versus thirty-six cents expected — and importantly, even excluding the eleven cent tariff refund tailwind, they still would have beaten at forty-two cents. Sales missed at nine twenty-three versus nine forty-three, but orders rose three and a half percent year-over-year. Full-year EPS guidance was left unchanged. This is a solid print with mixed optics on revenue.

THOR Industries is the ugliest print this morning. They missed on earnings per share — seventy-eight cents versus eighty-seven cents expected — as gross margins collapsed 230 basis points year-over-year to twelve point four percent. Management's language was cautious, pointing to stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation weighing on household budgets. They won't give formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall. The one bright spot is the North American towable RV order backlog, which surged roughly seventy-five percent year-over-year. Watch this as a read on the consumer discretionary stress picture.

Finally, Viking Therapeutics is the name to watch in pre-market. Shares are spiking after the company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735 — twenty-two percent weight loss. That's a headline number that will get attention in the obesity drug space and could reprice the whole GLP-1 competitive landscape intraday.

Bottom line for the session: no broad macro catalyst in this note, so the tape will trade on its own technical momentum. Viking is the high-beta momentum play. AutoZone could see selling pressure on the quality-of-beat concern. THOR is a macro tell on the stretched consumer. Stay disciplined.
